headline: 15 Stolen Greek Treasures Spanning 5,000 Years Return Home
meta_description: Millions in ancient Greek artifacts looted decades ago were identified at the Met and returned to Greece through a major antiquities trafficking investigation.
summary_short: New York authorities returned 15 ancient Greek artifacts worth millions to Greece, including bronze helmets from 700 BCE and pieces dating back to 2,700 BCE.
body:
Fifteen ancient Greek artifacts worth millions of dollars—smuggled out of Greece over decades and laundered through false documentation at the Metropolitan Museum of Art—have been ceremonially returned to their homeland. The collection spans five millennia, from a marble figurine dating to 2,700 BCE to bronze helmets and belly guards from the late 7th century BCE. Greece's Minister of Culture, Lina Mendoni, accepted the pieces at a handover in Manhattan on September 21st, noting that some would be reunited with finds from the same archaeological excavations in Crete's Iraklio museum. The five bronze objects—two helmets and three mitrai—were traced to looting at a sanctuary on the hill of Prophet Elias in Afrati, Crete, between 1964 and 1966. One helmet bears extraordinary embossed details of flowers, dogs, and a winged figure holding a serpent. These pieces alone are valued at more than $2 million.

The investigation, led by Manhattan's Antiquities Trafficking Unit, represents part of a much larger effort to dismantle cultural property crime networks. Among the 15 returned items were also a terracotta jug looted from burial grounds in the Argolis-Corinthia region and smuggled through Switzerland and the United Kingdom before reaching the Met, along with bronze and gold bracelets and a marble bust of a Roman emperor.

What the recovery reveals is a systemic problem: despite the Met's cooperation, investigators found themselves repeatedly identifying looted artifacts that should never have entered the museum in the first place. The Manhattan District Attorney's Antiquities Trafficking Unit has now convicted 18 individuals of cultural property crimes and recovered over 6,400 treasures valued at $490 million—returning more than 6,150 items to 39 countries. This work shows that justice for stolen heritage remains possible, even across decades.
quick_facts: 15 ancient Greek artifacts returned from Metropolitan Museum of Art
Objects span 5,000 years, from 2,700 BCE to Roman era
Five bronze helmets and belly guards worth $2 million from Crete
Looted between 1964–1966 from sanctuary at Prophet Elias, Crete
Manhattan DA has recovered $490 million in cultural treasures since
